Your weekend is forty-eight hours long, so why does it feel like ten minutes?
Meanwhile, a Monday meeting can last a year, and it's made of the exact same minutes.
Your brain has no clock you can read.
Scientists think it guesses, by counting how often you pay attention to time.
At your desk, you check the clock again and again, so the seconds pile up.
On a Saturday, you're busy, you forget to look, and the counting stops.
Fewer counted seconds feels like less time, even though the real clock never slowed.
Sunday night still arrives exactly on schedule.
Want a longer weekend? Try watching the clock. It works great, and ruins everything.
And why does the first day of a holiday last forever?
